headline: East Maui water contested case start moved to January 19

meeting.summary: A county attorney said the East Maui water contested case will start January 19, with hearings open in person but not livestreamed.
meeting.recap: The board held a special meeting on October 16, 2026, online through Teams.[[0:00:36]] A county attorney for the Department of Water Supply updated the board on East Maui Irrigation's contested case (a court-like hearing).[[0:03:46]] She said the contested case will now start January 19.[[0:05:23]] All November and December dates are canceled, except a possible site visit not yet scheduled.[[0:06:40]] The hearing officer ruled the hearings will be open to the public in person, as space allows, but not livestreamed.[[0:07:14]] Named witnesses may not watch the hearings before they testify.[[0:08:10]] Main witness testimony will be filed in writing as sworn statements, then tested by cross-examination.[[0:09:40]] She said main issues include how much water is requested, county water needs, Native Hawaiian uses, and fire protection.[[0:10:23]] She said no estimate has been given for when a recommendation will reach the board.[[0:16:24]] She offered to summarize witnesses and issues, possibly at the board's December meeting.[[0:18:17]] The chair said whether to ask for a board member on the site visit will go on the next agenda.[[0:22:24]] The water department is seeking a Maui room, such as the planning conference room, for some hearings.[[0:22:50]] The next meeting is November 6, 2026.[[0:25:14]]
meeting.next: The county attorney said she will share hearing dates with everyone once she has them. The county attorney said a special meeting in early January could be held to share the witness summary. The chair said she would put the site-visit question on the agenda for the next meeting.
